title: The man who argued with God

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever spoken up for someone who wasn’t there to speak for themselves?
options: then you already know a little of how this man felt. listen.
most of us carry one of those. listen.
then this story might give you the nerve. listen.

steps.line: In the heat of the day, an old man named Abraham sat at the door of his tent. Three strangers appeared on the road.
He ran to meet them and fed them: fresh bread, a tender calf, curds and milk. He stood by them under the tree while they ate.
As the guests left, Abraham walked with them, looking down toward Sodom. Then God told him: the outcry against that city is great. I will go and see.
Abraham came closer. “Will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked? Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly?”

steps.q: The Hebrew says Abraham “came near.” The old rabbis asked: near for what?
o: To whisper, so the guests wouldn’t hear
To fight, to make peace, and to pray
To bow down and beg for mercy
steps.why: In the midrash, one sage says he came near for battle, another for peace, another for prayer. A fourth says: all three.

steps.line: “What if there are fifty good people in the city?” And God said: for fifty, I will spare the whole place.

steps.q: God agrees: for fifty good people, the city will be spared. What does Abraham do now?
o: Pushes on, for fewer and fewer
Asks God to spare it for just one
Asks God to warn the city first
steps.why: He keeps going. Forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty. Politely, and stubbornly.

steps.line: So Abraham kept going: forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty, calling himself “but dust and ashes.” He stopped at ten. For ten, God said, I will not destroy it.

steps.q: Abraham calls himself “dust and ashes,” and keeps asking anyway. What does that show?
o: He was frightened, so he gave in
He was trying to flatter God
He was humble and brave at the same time
steps.why: Humble about himself, stubborn for others. He asked nothing for himself, only for a whole city.

steps.q: Why did Abraham stop at ten? Rashi gives a surprising answer.
o: Noah’s family of eight hadn’t saved a world
Ten was all the time God would give him
steps.why: Rashi notes the flood came though Noah’s household numbered eight, so Abraham dared go no lower than ten. Ten is also a minyan, the group for communal prayer.

steps.line: Today, many Jews still speak up for people who aren’t in the room. Arguing for justice, even with heaven, is part of the tradition.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. god never tells abraham to be quiet. every round, god listens and answers.
in jewish tradition, arguing with god isn’t the opposite of faith. moses argues later, and so does job. abraham did it with respect, and for other people.

steps.q: When Abraham asks, “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly?”, what is he really doing?
o: Reminding God of God’s own justice
Asking to be the judge himself
steps.why: He isn’t doubting God. He’s trusting that God cares about justice, enough to ask God to live up to it.

today.say: think of someone who isn’t in the room when things are decided about them. today, speak up for them once, kindly and directly. that’s how abraham did it.
options: direct, respectful, and for someone else. that’s abraham.
he called himself dust and ashes, and still spoke. start small.

tomorrow.line: a man alone by a river at night, dreading tomorrow. what happens before sunrise gives a whole people its name.
